lines.en: Already a week since Yoo Joonghyuk disappeared.
In that time, the atmosphere within <Kim Dokja’s Company> had changed a little.
People spoke noticeably less. Rather than expressing themselves or talking to one another, they silently devoted themselves to training.
Jung Heewon was one of them. She mingled with the others, practicing her skills and training her body······ or pretended to. More precisely, she was gauging one particular person’s mood.
“Ah, I seriously can’t take this anymore! How long are we going to keep this up?”

At Jung Heewon’s words, Lee Hyunsung flinched while using [Great Mountain Push] against the ground, and Shin Yoosung’s shoulders shook as she practiced [Advanced Diverse Communication]. The most startled was Lee Jihye, who had been practicing [Kendo].
Jung Heewon pressed her.
“You, Jihye! Are you never going to speak to Dokja-ssi again?”
“······I don’t know.”
“You’re still angry? Whatever happened, you have to talk about it.”
Lee Jihye snapped and shouted,

“I’m not angry! Thinking about it, it wasn’t even that big a deal······. Something similar happened with the Prophets, didn’t it? I know he’s a good person, too. ······I just didn’t like the word ‘character’!”
Already a week, too, since Kim Dokja dropped that bombshell on his companions.
They had each thought about his words in their own way.
To summarize, it had gone something like this.
On the first day, everyone was shocked.
On the second, they began to think something like this had already happened. (Jung Heewon: “Come to think of it, with the constellations around, it’s the same either way.”)
On the third, someone thought about it further and found it fascinating that she appeared in a novel. (Lee Seolhwa: “How important a role did I have?”)
On the fourth, someone suggested that, if Kim Dokja had read such a novel, he might be this world’s god after all. (Lee Gilyoung: “I knew you were a god, hyung.”)
On the fifth, someone finally argued that Kim Dokja was the one who needed comfort right now, rather than them. (Shin Yoosung: “Maybe he’s having the hardest time of all right now.”)
Lee Hyunsung, who had listened to the entire conversation, spoke.
“I certainly can’t imagine how Dokja-ssi must feel right now. And Joonghyuk-ssi disappeared a few days ago, too······.”
The companions nodded, seeming to agree.
In the end, their gazes focused on Lee Jihye again.
“Jihye.”
Her face turning red, Lee Jihye yelled,
“I’m telling you! He looks absolutely miserable. How am I supposed to talk to him?”
“Even so.”
“Then why did Dokja-ajusshi have to say anything······? He could’ve just kept deceiving us like he always······.”
“Jihye.”
At Jung Heewon’s call, Lee Jihye flinched and lowered her head.
Jung Heewon continued.
“We can’t dismiss Dokja-ssi’s choice just because we don’t understand it. I don’t know the details, but it must have been something he needed to do. He must have had his reasons.”
“······Do you think we’re just ‘characters,’ too, unnie?”
“I don’t know that, either. But······ we’re already living through ‘scenarios.’ What does it matter whether we’re characters or not? It’s not Dokja-ssi’s fault that a novel like that existed.”
She was right.
Kim Dokja hadn’t made the world this way. He was simply the only reader who happened to read that novel.
Characters in a novel······. So what? They had already been the constellations’ clowns since these damned scenarios began. Hearing it now didn’t make it feel any more real.
After chewing her lip for a long time, Lee Jihye spoke.
“All right. I’ll go talk to him. But Yoosung and Hyunsung-ajusshi are coming with me.”
At her words, Lee Hyunsung and Shin Yoosung looked at each other and hesitated.
“Uh, well. Actually, I went last night······.”
“I talked to him three days ago.”
Lee Jihye swept her gaze over the companions, and her face went pale.
“······What? So I’m the only one who hasn’t gone?”
I had mixed feelings as I received the companions who visited me one by one.

Lee Seolhwa would suddenly appear in the middle of the night and hook a Story Pack up to my perfectly healthy arm. Or I would wake in the morning to find things like the hind legs of enormous monsters and creatures of the insect king species outside my door.
I was the one who had done something wrong, yet they were taking care of me. I didn’t know how to respond.
—If we’re characters, Dokja-ssi, you’ve thrown yourself into danger for those characters so many times. That’s all I’m going to remember. The others, too.
That was what Jung Heewon said.
—Ajusshi, I’m young, so I don’t really understand why you said that. But······ I know you’re having a very hard time right now.
That was what Shin Yoosung and Lee Gilyoung said.
—Dokja-ssi, my manual has no procedure for handling this situation. So please stop making things so difficult for me and go back to your usual self.
Lee Hyunsung was Lee Hyunsung, as always.
—I’m not good at apologizing or comforting people. If I really appear in that novel, you should know that, ajusshi, right?
And even Lee Jihye······.
Some comfort gathers like warm drops of spring rain.
So quietly that you don’t even recognize it as comfort.
Snow was piling up beneath the city walls. Winter already setting in.

I looked down at the citizens busily clearing the snow. The world had turned upside down and monsters ran rampant, but the snow still had to be cleared. Left too long, it would eventually turn into hard ice and become a nuisance.
“Are your preparations going well?”
I turned to find Kyrgios floating beside me in the lotus position. Having fully recovered his vigor, he had recently taken charge of teaching the companions martial arts.
“We’re working hard.”
The coming ‘Great War of Saints and Demons’ was scenario eighty. And the highest scenario we could currently access through the ‘Context of the Constellations’ was sixty-five.

In other words, we had to build up enough Stories in the time remaining to clear scenario sixty-five and advance to the second Context of the Constellations. Only then would <Kim Dokja’s Company> qualify for scenario eighty.
“We’re steadily accumulating Stories, and the scenarios are going smoothly. Apart from <Gigantomachia>, the scenarios in the sixties are all about the same difficulty.”
「Demon Realm’s Spring」, and now 「Torch That Swallowed the Myth」 as well.

With a level of probability unlike anything we’d had before, we cleared scenarios with unstoppable momentum. We were flying so high that we couldn’t find a nebula to match us in the scenarios in the sixties.
As we also began the advertising we’d promised the ‘Mass Production Maker,’ <Kim Dokja’s Company>’s stock rose by the day.
Right on cue, the ‘Mass Production Maker’s’ advertisement played on a panel in the air.
—Scenarios. Those countless roads.
As my voice delivered the monologue, several cars on the screen sped along dimensional roads toward portals.
But there was one car that chose not to take a portal: the [X-grade Ferrarghini] carrying Han Sooyoung.
—Everyone has a road of their own.
The [X-grade Ferrarghini], cutting across the scattering cars and driving straight out into the darkness.
The camera closed in on Han Sooyoung’s face, emphasizing the beauty mark beneath her eye, as her lips synced to my voice.
—But a truly strong person drives down a road that isn’t a road.
The ‘Mass Production Maker’ logo appearing as the screen faded to black.
A bitter taste filled my mouth.
That old man really was something. He’d scared me about it before, and now he was using it as advertising copy.
There was no way an ad like that would work on the constellations······.
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ likes this advertisement.]
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ wants an ‘X-grade Ferrarghini.’]
[Your advertisement has stimulated some constellations’ desire to purchase.]
······Except it did.
Watching the advertisement beside me, Kyrgios clicked his tongue. Apparently, the transcendent from Murim couldn’t accept the conveniences of modern civilization.
“I don’t understand. You could run much faster with martial arts than by riding a machine like that.”
“That’s true.”
“Breaking the Sky’s brat of a disciple still hasn’t returned, has he?”
I fell silent at the sudden question.
Among Breaking the Sky Sword Saint’s disciples, there was only one he could be calling that brat.
“He’s perfectly capable of finding his own way to survive. I’m not worried.”
I was worried.
Worried he might be off acting like a sunfish somewhere again.
Or that his depression might suddenly return and make him consider regressing.
Even as I reminded myself that few beings could touch Yoo Joonghyuk as he was now, I couldn’t completely suppress my anxiety.
But for now, I could only trust him.
Just as I always had back when I knew him only through words on a page.
“When we reach the next scenario area, he’ll pop up out of nowhere again. That’s just the kind of guy he is.”
“‘Reincarnation Island’ will not be easy.”
“I know.”
I nodded as I spoke.
Kyrgios was a transcendent, and he had visited ‘Reincarnation Island’ before.
Kyrgios looked below the battlements. A little apart from the others, Jang Hayoung stood alone, silently throwing straight punches.
“Take Hayoung with you on this journey. That one has inherited Breaking the Sky’s true teachings as well. Hayoung won’t be a burden.”
“I was planning to.”

Jang Hayoung was essential to this scenario. In the original novel, ‘Reincarnation Island’ was also where Hayoung acquired the name ‘King of Transcendents.’ I gave a little wave. Hayoung, who had been looking this way, promptly turned away.
I looked at the distant sky again.
Inside my sleeve, I could feel the ticking vibration of the watch hands.
······Twenty-one days until the Great War of Saints and Demons.
I quietly turned on my smartphone and opened the Ways of Survival file.
I had hurt my companions because of this novel. Yet it was also thanks to this novel that I had come to know them.
Amid those conflicting emotions, I opened the ‘Great War of Saints and Demons’ section and began to read.
The first sentence of the ‘Great War of Saints and Demons’ began like this.
「At last, the season of ruin was slowly approaching this world as well.」
The nebula <Eden>.
For some reason, angels crowded the entrance to a training ground that would ordinarily have been deserted.
[Ah, that incarnation is the one······.]
[······That’s a human body?]

Inside the training ground they were peering into, a shirtless man held a sword and glared at the air. At first glance, he seemed merely to be holding it, but he was actually cutting through the air. An angel with keen eyes could see that the blade was moving downward at an infinitesimal speed.
It was the training Yoo Joonghyuk repeated whenever he wanted to forget time.
Stretching a fleeting instant out, sensing the eternity woven into every thread of it.

The air stirred violently around movements imbued with strict discipline. His Status, restrained like a crouching dragon. But to say something was restrained was also to say that something had yet to erupt.
[Impressive. As you are now, even most Narrative-grade constellations would not dare attack you carelessly.]
Yoo Joonghyuk frowned and turned to find a pale-faced archangel.
The one who recorded everything in <Eden>.
At Yoo Joonghyuk’s look, which seemed to ask why he was here, Metatron smiled wryly.
[I came to offer a little advice. If you intend to keep removing your shirt every time you train, perhaps you could choose another location······.]
“<Eden>’s probability density is best suited to this training.”
[That is your concern. But your indecent exposure is affecting the young angels······.]
“Metatron. Why did you show me that ‘revelation’?”
Faced with someone who ignored everything said to him, Metatron smacked his lips and changed the subject.
[I believe I told you it was a transaction. Payment for your taking the side of ‘Good’ in the ‘Duet between Good and Evil.’ Nothing more, nothing less.]
“Rather than an attempt to divide <Kim Dokja’s Company>?”
[Why would <Eden> do such a thing?]
“I know how closely you’re watching Kim Dokja. You must be trying to keep his forces from growing.”
[Is that why you are staging a shirtless protest here?]
“You don’t understand a word I say.”

Metatron shook his head as though uncertain which of them that described. Regardless, Yoo Joonghyuk continued swinging his sword at the air. Very slowly, as if driving it into an imaginary opponent to snuff out their life.
[If you intend to continue this unlawful protest, formally leave <Kim Dokja’s Company> and join <Eden>. Then I can permit you to remove your shirt—]
“Give me the next page of the ‘revelation.’ Is that all the information you have?”
[Do you not think I might give you false information?]
“You’d be better than those demon king bastards who lie through their teeth.”
[······So that is why you invaded our <Eden> instead of following Asmodeus?]
“If the demon kings know something, you should know it, too.”
Metatron still hadn’t forgotten the day Yoo Joonghyuk had invaded <Eden> alone.

Making a scene at the entrance to the great barrier guarded by Powers and Virtues. Even the demon kings didn’t do that. In fact, if Metatron hadn’t intervened, Michael would have taken Yoo Joonghyuk’s head that day.
Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
“Enough talk. Give me the revelation. Isn’t it enough that I’ve played along with your schemes this far?”
Metatron’s lips twisted bitterly. A cold gleam flashed through his eyes as he quietly studied Yoo Joonghyuk.
[Incarnation Yoo Joonghyuk. Strictly speaking, the information I gave you was not a ‘revelation.’ It was information received from a special being.]
“A special being?”
[Do you really wish to know?]
After watching Yoo Joonghyuk for a moment, Metatron slowly raised his head. Yoo Joonghyuk followed his gaze.
For an instant, it felt as though the sky over <Eden> was warping into pitch-black darkness.
Some of the angels gathered around the training ground gave little screams and sank to the ground.
Yoo Joonghyuk instinctively gripped his [Black Heavenly Demon Sword].
······A demon king? No.
Rather than demonic power (魔), it was something closer to chaos.
[Your constellation sponsor feels uneasy about the alien being.]
When he blinked again, the scenery around him had changed.
The heart of the <Star Stream>. Formless darkness coiled within the pitch-black universe.
A great being (大存在) that even the transcendent Yoo Joonghyuk struggled to look at.
Yoo Joonghyuk asked,
“Who are you?”
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ looks at the incarnation ‘Yoo Joonghyuk.’]
The darkness spoke.
【It has been a while, puppet of the Oldest Dream.】
Time passed swiftly that winter.
Having rapidly cleared the scenarios through number sixty-five, <Kim Dokja’s Company> had reached the second ‘Context of the Constellations’ a week earlier.
At last, we had fulfilled the minimum requirements to challenge ‘scenario eighty.’
[The advertising payment from the ‘Mass Production Maker’ has arrived.]
[You have received 2,500,000 coins.]
The nebula’s balance was growing quickly, too. Two and a half million coins from a single advertisement. The [X-grade Ferrarghini] seemed to be selling quite well.
We had agreed to receive an ongoing share of the sales revenue, so more income would follow.
“It’s about time.”
And finally, the day of the scenario.
I looked back at the companions who had finished preparing.
Lee Hyunsung, Jung Heewon, Lee Jihye, Shin Yoosung and Lee Gilyoung. And Jang Hayoung as well······.
“Dokja-ssi, are you sure it’s all right for us to leave like this?”
Lee Hyunsung spoke as though something worried him.
I understood. Exactly a week earlier, I had instructed everyone to do nothing and rest until ‘scenario eighty’ opened.
“With discipline this lax······.”
Lax discipline, huh.
So said the true soldier with a history of losing both cartridge cases and a safety pin.
“Nothing we do now will let us catch up to the highest-Status constellations. What matters is what we do there, not what we do here. ······By the way, I feel like someone’s missing.”
“Sooyoung-ssi went ahead. She said she doesn’t follow orders······.”
Honestly, this company didn’t have a single obedient employee.
Well, Han Sooyoung would find a way to survive on her own.
When I turned, Mother and the wanderers were watching us from the [Industrial Complex]’s main gate.
“We’ll be off, then.”
“Take care.”
I left Seoul’s security to Mother and the wanderers. People with little ambition for the later scenarios, all of them. They had decided to build lives in their own ways rather than clear scenarios.
Lee Seolhwa and Gong Pildu, who had agreed to oversee the recent influx of incarnations, had also decided to remain in Seoul.
“Please look after Seoul.”
Lee Seolhwa nodded.
Across the square, Gong Pildu was surrounded by incarnations tackling the early scenarios, explaining something in a brusque voice.
“What matters is securing a good location first. You have to get your hands on good land before anyone else! Got that?”
······I hoped things would be all right.
—Breaking the Sky Sword Saint and I will join you later. Go ahead.
I nodded back at Kyrgios, who was watching from a distance, then signaled into the air.
A low-grade dokkaebi in charge of scenario transfers soon appeared.
[<Kim Dokja’s Company>. Are your preparations complete?]
“Begin the transfer.”
As the low-grade dokkaebi chanted, we were sucked into the portal beneath our feet.
It must have been a fairly high-quality portal. I felt no dizziness even as space and time changed. How much time passed?
[You have entered the waiting room for scenario eighty.]
In place of Gwanghwamun’s peaceful scenery, a waiting room paved with pale marble appeared. It seethed with the excitement of the constellations and incarnations who had arrived before us.
[When does the scenario start?]
[Hurry up and open it! We don’t have all day!]
Among the constellations were some whose faces I knew well.
Brash Swamp Predator. I hadn’t seen that one since the ‘Demon King Selection’ and had assumed they were dead, but apparently they were still alive.
Behind me, Jung Heewon murmured,
“There seem to be a lot of formidable constellations here.”
“Ajusshi, Ranveer Khan and Fei Hu are over there, too!”
“I can see <Papyrus> and <Tamna> as well.”
The members of <Kim Dokja’s Company>, huddled close behind me like penguins enduring the cold. They also resembled country people newly arrived in Seoul.
Lee Jihye stuck out her lip and snapped,
“Ajusshi, what are you grinning about?”
“You should smile while you still can, too.”
In the distance, some constellations from <Olympus> waved at us.
Dionysus and Aphrodite. Surely they weren’t here to perform again.
Behind them, I could see some constellations from <Vedas>, along with Surya, the ‘Supreme God of Light.’
Perhaps Anna Croft or Yoo Joonghyuk was somewhere among them, too.
[The Demon King ‘Duke of Everywhere’ glares at you.]
[The Demon King ‘Eyes that See the Forbidden’ watches you warily.]
······As expected, those bastards were here, too.
[The constellation ‘Guardian of Youths and Travel’ yawns as though bored.]
[The constellation ‘Savior of Corruption’ directs a ferocious aura toward you.]
Even the archangels of <Eden>.
By scenario eighty, the sheer scale was certainly different.
We would now have to compete against those terrifying Narrative-grade constellations.
A dokkaebi floated up at the center of the great square. It was Bihyung.
[Everyone has gathered, I see. I am Bihyung, the dokkaebi who will be hosting this scenario.]
Normally, a great dokkaebi would host a scenario of this scale. Since Bihyung was here, his standing within the [Bureau] must have risen considerably.

[The ‘Great War of Saints and Demons’ was originally scheduled for a different venue. But due to special circumstances, ‘Reincarnation Island’ has been selected as the scenario area this time. Well, you know how our bigwigs up top are.]
Some constellations snickered.
Jokes insulting the <Star Stream> or the [Bureau] always went over well, no matter where you were.
That bastard Bihyung didn’t seem afraid of probability at all.
[Some of you may find this stage unfamiliar. It is a very old place, and hardly used anymore. You could say it was left behind by the times······.]
As Bihyung spoke, a video began playing on the screen overhead.
It showed ‘Reincarnation Island,’ the stage for the scenario about to begin.
[We came to participate in the ‘Great War of Saints and Demons.’ We don’t care where it happens!]
[I’m not expecting much. It’ll obviously be another setting full of Sword Masters and Great Wizards.]
The constellations sneered as though they’d already experienced the scenario.
Then Bihyung spoke.
[Sword Masters······. You can put those worries to rest this time. This setting is rather special.]
The constellations murmured at his words.
Bihyung continued.
[When ‘this island’ first opened, there were no Sword Masters, no Great Wizards, and not even the concept of circles. That is how old this island is.]
Many constellations listened closely.
The members of the ‘Gourmet Association’ showed particular interest.
They probably knew something about the island.

[Well, you’ll understand the details once you experience them. First, I’ll explain what you need to know for the scenario. Before advancing to the ‘Main Island,’ the stage of the ‘Great War of Saints and Demons,’ you will experience a tutorial area.]
A rough map of the island appeared on the screen.
An enormous island floating in the heart of the universe, surrounded by an archipelago of smaller islands (群島).
Bihyung pointed to the outermost islands as he spoke.

[You will begin on the ‘Small Islands’ at the edges. Through the tutorial here, you will learn how to adapt to the island, then receive a scenario that allows you to advance to the ‘Main Island,’ the principal stage of the ‘Great War of Saints and Demons.’]
From the explanation, it seemed that the usual rules of ‘Reincarnation Island’ still applied.
That was welcome news to me.
To the other constellations, of course, it wasn’t.
[A tutorial? We’re constellations. Are you joking?]
[Oh, of course it’s only called a tutorial. You aren’t required to do it. There are plenty of ways to advance straight to the ‘Main Island,’ so please don’t be so angry.]
Usually, when a dokkaebi talked like that, it meant that skipping the tutorial would make the scenario go to shit.
If the constellations here knew what would actually happen on those islands, about half would probably withdraw their applications.
Perhaps noticing my gaze, Bihyung looked my way and winked.

[A scenario is best when it starts without an explanation. I’ve rambled on too long. Now, please choose the ‘Small Island’ where you will begin. Those who wish to start on the same island may choose the same one.]
As Bihyung finished, the constellations began choosing their starting points.
The companions and I chose the same island. There was no reason to split up when we could go together.
I saw some constellations glance around, then follow my choice of island.
······So that was how they intended to play it from the start.
I looked at the companions and spoke.
“You all remember what I said yesterday, right?”
Jung Heewon answered.
“You told us to run toward the center of the island when the scenario began?”
“Yes. Don’t even think about fighting anyone else. Just run and find the village in the center of the island.”
This scenario was completely different from anything we had experienced so far. If they approached the tutorial in the usual way, even my companions wouldn’t survive.
Perhaps because they knew I’d read Ways of Survival, they no longer questioned my suggestions. It left me with a bitter feeling of guilt.
Once all the constellations had finished preparing, Bihyung’s message rang out.
[The scenario transfer will now begin!]
I drew [Unbreakable Faith] from inside my clothes.
In this scenario, every minute and second it took to draw your sword mattered.
“Everyone, I’ll see you in the village.”
At the same time, the companions and I turned into clusters of light.
[A new main scenario has arrived!]
[Main Scenario #80 — ‘Reincarnation Island’ has begun.]
Amid the flood of messages, my darkened surroundings grew bright.
The smell of vegetation stung my nose. I had been thrown into the island’s forest. None of the companions were nearby. They had probably all been transported to different places on the island.
[You are currently in the exploration area of ‘Island 531.’ Find the village with a guide.]
[Hidden Scenario — ‘Survival Game’ has begun!]
And almost simultaneously, a dokkaebi’s message pouring down from the sky.
[It wouldn’t be fun like this, would it? Survival is the best way to start. Constellations, enjoy feeling as though you’ve returned to the old days in this fierce struggle for survival!]
<Hidden Scenario — Survival Game>
Category: Hidden
Difficulty: SSS
Clear Conditions: Avoid the competitors who entered with you and reach the island’s village, or kill your competitors.
Time Limit: 24 hours
Reward: 50,000 coins, tutorial area clear.
Failure: Death
I knew it.
There was no way the dokkaebis who had specifically chosen this island as the stage would leave it at that.
Almost simultaneously, I sensed an ominous presence nearby. It was already too late to hide.
[The Demon King ‘Magic Peacock of Geometry’ shows hostility toward you!]
A being that emerged from the undergrowth. One of the demon kings who had followed me.
The sixty-fifth-ranked Demon King, ‘Magic Peacock of Geometry,’ Andrealphus.
[Demon King of Salvation. I hear you defeated the Demon King Amdusias?]
Deep blue demonic flames blazed in the hands of the brilliantly feathered creature. Andrealphus was a demon king said to have mastered every kind of magic to perfection.
[Do not get carried away just because you defeated a single stallion.]
Resembling a peacock, he rattled off words through his pointed beak, then charged at me while chanting a spell. Apparently, he had chosen me as his first prey.
I ran toward him as well.
Andrealphus muttered,
[Your footwork is dreadful, and your skill proficiency is laughably low. You’re no better than an ordinary human. You defeated Amdusias with so little?]
Regardless, I kept running hard. I wasn’t even using [Way of the Wind], so my steps were much slower than usual.
Andrealphus sneered.
[Die.]
The magic he activated: [Hellfire], a ninth-circle spell. Literally borrowing the flames of hell, it was a great spell that even I couldn’t survive unscathed if it hit me head-on.
But the moment he activated it, something strange happened.
Fsssh.
The Hellfire that should have burned down the entire forest produced a small flame, then went out feebly.
[The island’s probability does not permit the spell ‘Hellfire.’]
A bewildered Andrealphus looked sharply at me.
I was already right in front of him.
“They told you this island had no Sword Masters or Great Wizards.”
Andrealphus’ eyes widened in shock.
“So of course there wouldn’t be any ‘Hellfire,’ either, would there?”
He must have found it hard to believe.
But that was this island’s law.
A place ruled by the strongest probability in the <Star Stream>.
[A powerful force of probability is in effect on this island!]
[You cannot use the ‘Attributes Window’ on this island. All overall stats converted into system data are reset.]
On this island, the system couldn’t be used.
[The use of most ‘skills’ created after the first generation is restricted on this island.]
[‘Stigma’ and ‘Story’ proficiency is reset on this island.]
Every combat technique acquired so far became useless.
Andrealphus’ expression froze as he belatedly tried to recite the incantation for a defensive skill.
Without any technique whatsoever, I crudely thrust my sword forward.
An attack containing neither a skill nor a stigma pierced the Demon King Andrealphus’ chest all too easily.
[Unbreakable Faith], several times heavier than usual.
My sword hand trembled.
He wasn’t the only one who had lost the benefits of overall stats.
In the sweltering forest, the hot sunlight burned my skin.
Sweating profusely, I pulled my sword from the demon king’s dead incarnation body. Perhaps because of my weak muscles, even holding it was a struggle.
“······This is why I don’t like old stories.”
A world with no Sword Masters, Great Wizards, system, or Attributes Window.
[Ancient Stories respond to your gaze.]
Reincarnation Island.
This was the graveyard of ‘first-generation Stories’ left behind in the stream of stars.
Lee Hyunsung thought.
Was this how his maternal grandfather, who he’d once heard had fought in the Vietnam War, had felt?
A forest dense with leaves. Hiding among trees with unnaturally thick trunks, Lee Hyunsung recalled his survival training.
‘Move to the nearby reed bed using a low crawl.’
Alternating between low and high crawls, Lee Hyunsung moved slowly through the forest. He wanted to run straight toward the open field, but quite a few groups of constellations were heading that way.
At the sudden sound of someone pushing through the undergrowth, Lee Hyunsung quickly hid behind a tree trunk and held his breath.
[I distinctly saw the Demon King of Salvation choose this island······.]
[If we hunt him down, how do we divide the spoils?]
[Whoever takes his head gets half.]
The sounds of murmuring constellations. All of them were after Kim Dokja. Lee Hyunsung wanted to leap out immediately, cut off their heads, and put them on display.
一Run straight toward the center of the island.
Kim Dokja had said it.
That was the only way to survive this damned survival game. A message from someone who knew this world’s future.
For a moment, he wondered if he should have asked Kim Dokja more about Ways of Survival.
The more information he had about the manual, the better.
What would become of his future self, what kind of life he would lead······.
‘······This is no time for pointless thoughts.’
Lee Hyunsung raised both hands and slapped his cheeks.
If Kim Dokja hadn’t told him, there would be a reason.
Now was the time to focus on the situation.
Rustle.
He heard movement nearby again.
He heard no voices.
Someone was approaching.
Cautious movements.
Someone with a fair grasp of the basics of cover and concealment. The sounds drew closer, little by little.
Rustle.
A position where he was bound to be discovered soon, unless the other person changed direction first.
Tensing, Lee Hyunsung drew a dagger from inside his clothes.
Kim Dokja had told them to avoid combat at all costs, but that wasn’t always possible.
‘If I can’t avoid them, I strike first.’
Over the past few years, training hard enough to cough up blood had made Lee Hyunsung far stronger.
He was no longer the ‘Soldier who Turned a Blind Eye to Injustice’ from the first scenario.
At last, the enemy came right up to him.
But something felt strange. The pattern of a special forces uniform, glimpsed through the sparse reeds.
Lee Hyunsung murmured instinctively,
“Heewon-ssi?”
“Waaah!”
The [Sword of Judgement] suddenly thrust through the grass. Lee Hyunsung instinctively bent at the waist to dodge it.
A moment later, Jung Heewon poked her head out of the undergrowth.
“Hyunsung-ssi? Oh, I’m sorry.”
“No, it’s all right. Are you okay?”
Encountering a companion in this desperate situation was an indescribable relief.
Once he caught his breath, he noticed two children clinging tightly to Jung Heewon’s waist.
Shin Yoosung and Lee Gilyoung.
Looking at their pale, drawn faces, Lee Hyunsung asked,
“What’s wrong with the children?”
“······I’m not sure, either. I only just found them. They seem to have seen something shocking.”
Something shocking.
There certainly was something peculiar about this island.
For some time now, [Hercules’ Shield], strapped to Lee Hyunsung’s back, had felt terribly heavy.
Normally, he wouldn’t even have noticed the item’s weight······.
Lifting Shin Yoosung onto his back with one hand, Lee Hyunsung spoke.
“I think we should head to the island’s center and meet Dokja-ssi first.”
“Which way is the center?”
“I heard it was in the direction of the rising smoke······."
He raised his head slightly to check their bearings and saw a wisp of smoke rising between the enormous trees.
Not very far away.
Lee Hyunsung began crawling along with Jung Heewon.
Perhaps because he was with a dependable companion, the heartbeat he felt through the dog tags seemed to beat to a different rhythm than before.
How long did they crawl?
Before long, they reached the edge of the forest. A broad field stretching out before them.
They weren’t far from the source of the smoke now.
The problem was that a number of groups were blocking the field.
Jung Heewon frowned and spoke.
“······Looks like they followed us, doesn’t it?”
Constellations, each armed with weapons and Star Relics, peering about as they searched near the field.
Among them was the group Lee Hyunsung had glimpsed earlier.
“He told us to run instead of fighting, so I think we should avoid them, but······.”
If they entered the field now, they would definitely be spotted.
They could go around through the forest, but there was no telling how long that would take.
Then Shin Yoosung spoke from his back.
“Ajusshi, over there······.”
Her trembling finger pointed toward the forest on the opposite side of the field.
Something was running out of it.
A rough, ferocious cry.
The creature that burst through the forest was a monster Lee Hyunsung knew well.
After all, it appeared regularly in countless fantasy comics and novels.
Jung Heewon asked,
“Isn’t that an ‘orc’? It’s too weak to be in a scenario in the eighties······.”
An orc.
A monster that appeared in countless works of fantasy as the archetypal ‘early-stage monster.’
“Come to think of it, we’ve never fought ‘orcs’ before.”
It was strange when he thought about it.
Orcs were monsters so famous that even ordinary people knew them.
Yet by scenario eighty, they had never encountered one.
The constellations in the field shouted.
[There’s a limit to how much you can insult us!]
[Is this trash all they’ve set loose?]
Apparently, they found it just as absurd.
Looking annoyed, one constellation punched at the charging orc as though a weapon wasn’t worth the trouble.
A monster whose entire body should normally have burst apart from that single punch.
But the next moment, something strange happened.
Crack!
The orc’s swinging stone axe shattered the constellation’s fist.
Before the bewildered constellation could shout anything, another stone axe flew in from somewhere.
Crunch!
The constellation’s head bursting apart on the spot.
The constellation’s incarnation body, collapsing in a daze as though it hadn’t even realized what had happened to it.
With a roar from the orc that had let out an unpleasant laugh, the field turned into a horrific slaughterhouse.
[Aaaaaaagh!]
Terrifying constellations said to shatter mountains and cleave seas.
Those constellations were being killed by just two orcs, their heads bursting and their bodies being torn apart.
Jung Heewon and Lee Hyunsung were both dazed.
The sight felt unreal.
They had died that easily? Constellations?
······To ‘orcs’?
Having torn apart some fifteen constellations in an instant, the orcs were approaching this part of the forest.
······Please, let me not run into any orcs.
I repeated that thought as I pushed through the dense forest.
I kept getting winded in the heat, and my steps were heavy.
I hadn’t walked very long, yet the sweat pouring from my whole body made me feel close to exhaustion.
I hadn’t known the absence of overall stats would make such a difference.
There really was no getting around a starting Constitution of one.
To make matters worse, the feeling that even my shoulders had grown narrower.
I wanted to believe I was imagining it, but this was the reality of the ‘island.’
Reincarnation Island.
The place where the oldest stories in the <Star Stream> gathered.
Here, every stat buff accumulated outside as data was removed.
In other words, this was a place where the body’s pure, innate abilities mattered most.
That was precisely why I had so easily defeated the sixty-fifth-ranked Demon King.

Most constellations neglected physical training after ascending to constellationhood. As a result, when they first entered this island, they made the mistake of misjudging their actual combat strength.
It was a relief that ‘Andrealphus,’ at least, wasn’t the physical type······.
[You have killed 1 competitor so far.]
[You can obtain an additional reward upon entering the safe zone.]
Trying not to miss the occasional message, I continued moving through the shade cast by the dense trees.
To avoid dehydration, I also buried my face in the occasional stream and gulped down water.
The water was so clear and cold that it felt as though it purified my soul.
“······First-generation water really is clear.”
It wasn’t as though I disliked old stories on principle.
As a reader, I actually preferred old stories.
Stories of heroes filled with dreams and adventure.
Fighting dragons in forgotten mountain ranges, or setting out to find a legendary sword with beautiful elves and valiant dwarves······.
The problem was that I was now inside one of those ‘old stories.’
A world where I couldn’t use the Attributes Window’s power, with no convenient functions at all.
Monsters weren’t the only danger here.
Without the effects of skills, immunity naturally declined. Cold and disease were threats, too.
In the original novel, entire groups of constellations had been wiped out by infectious diseases.
In fact, Ways of Survival contained the following sentence.

「Accustomed to the conveniences of the Attributes Window and the system, the constellations helplessly died without putting up a proper fight when confronted with a world their sensibilities could not read.」
Constellations who had reigned from the thrones of the <Star Stream>, resplendent in their power and prestige, died because they couldn’t overcome mere infectious diseases or orcs.
Some even took their own lives, unable to endure the humiliation.
It was ridiculous.
[The participants on Island 861 have been wiped out.]
[The participants on Island 1896 have been wiped out.]
······It had begun.
By now, terrible tragedies had probably engulfed the ‘Small Islands.’
Constellations dying to the low-grade monsters they had always dismissed······.
[Many constellations are greatly shocked by the difficulty of ‘Reincarnation Island.’]
[Many constellations send messages of protest to the ‘Bureau’!]
Protesting was useless.
That was simply the kind of island this was.
Demon King, archangel······. A place where anyone who let their guard down for even a moment would lose their head.
Croak.
At the cry from the nearby undergrowth, I instinctively held my breath.
As far as I knew, only one kind of monster on this island cried like that.
A dwarfish monster with light green skin, about half my height.
······A ‘goblin’?
I barely managed a sigh of relief.
If it was a goblin rather than an orc, I had a chance as long as I kept my wits about me.
Kieeeee!
An ear-splitting shriek.
I instinctively swung my sword toward the cry.
Perhaps because my Strength was so poor, my body was dragged along in the direction [Unbreakable Faith] swung.
Fsssh!
Fortunately, the first goblin to leap up was struck by my blind swing and tumbled to the ground.
The trouble began after that.
「One law of the first generation: goblins never move alone.」
Two goblins leaped off their wounded companion, closing the distance in an instant and swinging spiked clubs.
Riiip!
One club left a long scrape along the outside of my thigh.
Damn it······. They’d said goblins were scarier than Demon Kings here.
[Exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ activates!]
Even then, without the [Fourth Wall], I might have panicked under the goblins’ barrage and died like the other constellations.
That was when an ominous voice rang out.
[The ‘island administrator’ expresses concern over the unfairness of the skill you are using.]
[The ‘island administrator’ declares that the skill cannot be used here.]
[The <Star Stream>’s probability agrees with the administrator’s objection.]
Tzzzzzt······!
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ shows displeasure.]
「Kim Dok ja sor ry」
‘Huh?’
「On this is land I lose my strength」
With those last words, I felt as though part of the barrier around my mind was fading.
I could feel my dormant senses coming to life.
In that instant, I realized what was happening to me.
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ grows thinner.]
[Your mental strength, enhanced through the ‘Fourth Wall,’ returns to its original state.]
[Your physical pain, reduced through the ‘Fourth Wall,’ returns to its original state.]
······Goddamn it.
I swallowed the curses rising in my throat.
Of all times for the [Fourth Wall] to thin······.

Unfamiliar pain set in—pain I’d forgotten while absorbed in the fight. The scratches on my shins and forearms stung. The clammy discomfort of my sweat-soaked shirt grew even more vivid, and the heat in the forest made me dizzy.
If I’d known this would happen, I would have exercised more.
Whooosh!
A spiked club flying at me to smash my head.
I all but rolled across the ground to evade the goblin’s attack.
Kieeeee!
My joints creaked at the hasty movement.
Following my path of escape, the goblins hammered their clubs down as though playing whack-a-mole.
The scent of blood on the spiked clubs raised the fine hairs on the backs of my hands. Though it was certainly a smell I’d encountered before, it felt unfamiliar.
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ becomes very thin.]
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ shakes precariously.]
Panting, I scrambled to my feet and adjusted my grip on the sword.

The two goblins who had lost their companion surrounded me, their red eyes gleaming. The murderous intent to charge at me as soon as they saw an opening. The moment I read that desire, the fear of death struck me anew.
Beyond the [Fourth Wall], now as thin as a skim of ice, the emotions I’d turned away from began to surface one by one.
Was this what the story I’d been watching was like?
I steadied my trembling breaths.
I had to fight. I could fight.
All the other companions had fought against this fear, too.
I alone had used the wall to avoid the pain like a coward.
「Kim Dokja gripped ‘Unbreakable Faith’ with trembling hands.」
Think. A way to defeat the goblins with my body as it was now.
I couldn’t use skills. But I could use stigmas.
Their proficiency had reset, but stigma use was definitely possible.
The question was how those stigmas would take effect.
Watching an approaching goblin, I activated [Song of the Sword].
[This stigma is not your stigma.]
[This stigma’s effect is fixed at the minimum.]
「The second day of the month. Clear. Went out early to inspect the weapons.」
[Unbreakable Faith] emitted a faint radiance, then returned to normal.
Even a fire arrow would have been nice. Damn it.
The only consolation was that my sword felt a little lighter.
Kieek?
Mocking my resistance, the goblins immediately swung their spiked clubs. When club met sword, it felt as though my wrist would snap.
They looked pathetic, but their strength exceeded a human’s. Monsters perfectly adapted to surviving on this island.
A second club then flew toward my waist. It was too late to block with my sword.
Thwack!
I swung my foot and kicked the club away. The sensation of spikes piercing my sole. I bit my lip at the horrific pain. Smelling blood, the enraged goblins howled.
If stigmas wouldn’t work, I had to try the second method.
[The Giant Story ‘Demon Realm’s Spring’ responds to your will.]
On this island, skills were sealed and all stigma proficiency was reset.
But that didn’t mean there was no usable power at all.
[The Giant Story ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’ responds to your will.]
Something that had undoubtedly existed even in the first generation, before circles or aura.
‘Stories.’
[You cannot exercise control over these Stories with your current strength.]
[Your Stories reject your rule.]
The problem was that, with my strength drastically reduced, my Stories would no longer listen to me.
[The Giant Story ‘Demon Realm’s Spring’ looks at you with pity.]
[The Giant Story ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’ covets your weakened body.]
Instead, the raging flow of energy and blood made blood rise in my throat.
The goblins momentarily shrank back at the power of the Stories they sensed from me, but soon regained their momentum and charged.
Stigmas were no use, and Stories wouldn’t listen.
I gritted my teeth at the approaching goblins.
In the end, only the last method remained.
If possible, I’d intended to save this for the very last contingency.
The moment I steeled myself and raised my magic power.
Fsssh!
A dagger flew through the undergrowth and pierced a goblin’s head. The goblin collapsing forward with a thud. A figure then rushed in and took off the other goblin’s head with exquisite bladework.
Seeing the girl’s ponytail streaming beneath her cap, I sighed in relief.
“Are you okay, ajusshi?”
Lee Jihye was looking at me, her head and face caked with mud.
In truth, I hadn’t used [Song of the Sword] solely to fight the goblins.
As the system message said, [Song of the Sword] wasn’t my stigma. And whenever you used a stigma that wasn’t yours, its original owner would inevitably become aware of your presence.
“······Whew. Thank goodness it really was you, ajusshi.”
Lee Jihye spoke as she washed her face in the stream.
Judging by her appearance, she’d had a fairly rough time, too.
“What the hell is this place? Skills and stigmas are all useless. If I hadn’t trained with Grandpa Kyrgios, I’d have been dead ages ago.”
“Are you hurt anywhere?”
“No. I hid well. But why do you look like that?”
“It just happened.”
I gave a vague answer and applied the [Wound Ointment] I’d received from Lee Seolhwa in advance.
Getting hurt this badly just fighting goblins. I couldn’t even imagine how difficult the journey ahead would be.
Looking exasperated, Lee Jihye snatched the ointment away.
“Give it here. You haven’t put enough on the back of your shoulder.”
With deft hands, she slathered the ointment over my wounds.
“Gently. Press too hard and I might die.”
“Stop exaggerating. Were you always this scrawny, though, ajusshi?”
“I’ve just lost a little muscle mass.”
“Your shoulders look about the same width as mine, don’t they?”
My pride stung, and I immediately snatched the ointment back. Or tried to, but failed. Lee Jihye was stronger than me.
She spoke in warning.
“Move, and your shoulder will break.”
It had been a long time since I’d felt this helpless.
“There. All done.”
Despite the ‘first generation’s’ probability, Lee Seolhwa’s ointment worked quite well. Not dramatically so, but the wounds it soaked into were healing quickly.
Well, even the first generation had magic and martial arts.
After tending to the wounds, Lee Jihye and I continued through the forest.
Fortunately, we met no more monsters, but night was already approaching.
Judging the direction of the smoke rising from the island’s center, Lee Jihye spoke.
“······Looks like we’ll have to camp here tonight.”
I nodded. We could force ourselves to travel at night, but without even the [Night Vision] skill, a mistake might bring us face-to-face with something far worse than goblins.
[Night has fallen on the island.]
[Some system functions are restored at night.]
[The ‘Dokkaebi Bag’ function is now available.]

I immediately opened the ‘Dokkaebi Bag’ and bought what we needed for camping: two portable one-person shelters and safety devices to watch the perimeter. I also stocked up on recovery items for emergencies.
Accepting the items from me, Lee Jihye blinked.
“What? After all that talk about the first generation, we can still buy things like this?”
“In the end, it’s still a scenario for making coins.”
First generation, second, or third, the essence of a scenario was making money. Naturally, the ‘Dokkaebi Bag’ would be permitted.
Hammering away as she put up a tent, Lee Jihye looked at me as though I were hopeless and asked,
“You said you served in the army, ajusshi. Don’t you know how to put up a tent?”
“How long do you think it’s been since I was discharged? Why are you so good at it?”
“I was a Girl Scout in elementary school.”
······Come to think of it, Lee Jihye did have that bit of character background.
Watching me struggle under the reduced Strength penalty, she quickly put up my tent as well.
The forest was cold at night. We gathered twigs and lit a fire. Warming ourselves by the burning campfire, Lee Jihye and I each became lost in thought.
I hadn’t used [Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint], but I could sense that the huddled Lee Jihye was holding something back. I waited patiently.
Throwing a dry twig into the crackling flames, she finally gathered her courage.
“Ajusshi, can I ask you something?”
“Go ahead.”
“That novel. How long has it existed?”
Somehow, I had expected that question.
I decided to answer honestly.
“More than ten years.”
My memory was a little hazy, but I hadn’t forgotten the time when I first clicked on Ways of Survival.
“How am I described in it?”
It was only natural to be curious. I would have wondered the same thing in her place.
I took my time recalling the descriptions of Lee Jihye.
Maritime Admiral Lee Jihye.
The girl who drew her sword before anyone else to protect her companions.
Proud, but in truth more warmhearted than anyone. A character who acted strong on the outside while her wounds festered deepest within.
Trying not to touch her wounds, I chose the most delicate words I could and told her.
As she listened, Lee Jihye’s mouth fell open as though she’d just had a dubious fortune reading.
“It’s so accurate it’s creepy······. There’s that much detail?”
“It’s a pretty long novel.”
“Even so. How do you remember it in that much detail?”
“I read it carefully.”
“Still, you remember way too much······. It’s creepy.”
This brat—after I’d gone to the trouble of answering her.
“I was in middle school then, and reading that novel was my only hobby.”
“Ajusshi, in middle school? Pfft, then you were younger than me when you first read it? No way.”
“Everyone was fifteen once.”
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ nods.]
Lee Jihye snickered as though she’d heard something amusing.
“I guess you’re right. I was fifteen once, too.”
She looked wistfully down at her scabbard.
A small keyring dangling from the end of her scabbard.
Having read Ways of Survival, of course I knew what it was.
“Are you okay?”
“······You know about this keyring, too?”
“A little.”
“So much for privacy.”
The keyring she always carried had been a gift from the friend who died in the first scenario.
Old sentences from Ways of Survival flowed through my mind.
「“Jihye. Kill me. It’s all right.”」
Lee Jihye was still a ‘Scarred Sword Demon.’
Even if her attribute name changed someday, that fact would not.
She was a character who would never forget the price of the sin she had committed.
“Hey. What happens to me at the end of that novel?”
At her question, a story I had deliberately kept out of my thoughts for a long time flashed through my mind.
The ending of Ways of Survival that I knew.
Jingle.
That was when I heard a bell. A signal from the safety devices I’d set up in advance.
Soon, the bells began ringing in a terrifying, ear-splitting rhythm.
Jingle. Jingle. Jingle. Jingle.
Jingle. Jingle. Jingle. Jingle.
“Ajusshi.”
Something was rapidly approaching.
Judging by the intervals between the bells, it wasn’t a goblin or an orc. A far more powerful monster.
Judging the direction of the rising smoke, I spoke.
“You’ll survive to the end and be happy. You did in the novel, too.”
It was a lie.
But a novel was a ‘lie’ to begin with,
and I had lived until now to make my lie real.
“Run toward the village. I’ll buy you time.”
“No! You run, ajusshi! You’re weaker than me here, remember?”
“Even you can’t handle that monster. The two of us together couldn’t do it.”
At her current level, goblins were the limit of what Lee Jihye could handle.
I continued in a calm voice.
“Hurry to the village and ask for help. That’s the only way we both survive. You can move faster than me.”
“Go! I have a way to get away somehow!”
“······You mean it?”
“Of course. Have you forgotten who I am?”
Only then did she nod, apparently reassured.
“Just hold on! I’ll bring the others right back!”
Not even ten-odd seconds after Lee Jihye disappeared, an enormous green monster emerged from the undergrowth.
A monster over three meters tall, exuding a vicious presence.
······Damn it. Not an orc, but a ‘troll’ of all things?
Saying I had a way to escape had been a lie.
Even if she brought the others, we couldn’t fight a troll.
We would be lucky not to get wiped out.
Grrrrr······.
Spotting me, the troll grinned and bared its horrific teeth.
As though it had already smashed countless constellations’ heads on the way here, its iron club was thickly plastered with their fragments.
Smiling bitterly, I gripped my sword.
A single blow from that club would probably kill me on the spot.
If there was no one to help me, that is.
Grrrrrr!
In the first place, clearing this island through ordinary means was almost impossible.
And, as always, an impossible scenario had a hidden piece concealed within it.
If things followed the original novel, it was about time for one to appear······.
The moment the troll’s club rose high into the air, I heard something pierce flesh.
Thuuunk!
A familiar blade protruded through the troll’s belly. It was Lee Jihye.
“······I knew it. You liar.”
「The Maritime Admiral never abandons her companions, even if it means her death.」
This plan had been possible from the start because I trusted that side of Lee Jihye.
Roaring furiously, the troll pulled the long blade out with its hand. The wound healing in an instant.
Leaving her blade behind and standing beside me, Lee Jihye smiled and spoke.
“If we die, let’s die together, ajusshi.”
Watching the troll charge at us, I smiled as well.
Lee Jihye wouldn’t die.
The history of her unbowed life would save her in the end.
The troll’s club fell almost simultaneously with a sound from the forest.
······Help was here.
A silver longsword cutting through the darkness.
And I saw it clearly.
A pure blade, using neither sword energy nor Ether Blade, cutting off that terrifying troll’s head as though it were a toy.
「The first generation’s Forgotten People (忘者) favor the themes of ‘love,’ ‘friendship,’ and ‘romance’ above all.」
The first generation. One of the oldest Stories in the <Star Stream>.
An owner of that Story was speaking.
“······Giving up your life for a companion? This is the first case like that in three hundred eighty-one years.”
Looking closely, I saw that more than one person had appeared.
“See? I told you. They’re that sort of people.”
“So it was true. There are still some worthwhile stories left outside.”
Hearty laughter rang out. Something was strange. This hadn’t happened in the original novel? Then I saw the face of the being who walked out of the darkness.
“It has been a while, descendant. Three years by the outside world’s time?”
To my surprise, he was someone I already knew.
A well-groomed beard and spirited eyebrows.
Even the thick lips that revealed his characteristic upright nature.
The man who emerged from the darkness looked exactly as he had when I met him three years ago.
“······Goryeo’s First Sword?”
“I didn’t expect to meet you in a place like this, Kim Dokja.”
Cheok Jungyeong, a constellation of the Korean Peninsula, was on Reincarnation Island.
I owed Cheok Jungyeong a great deal, from [Dark Castle] to the [Demon King Selection].

I swallowed my rising delight. He was a good constellation, but I didn’t yet know why he was here. First, I needed to learn his purpose. If it conflicted with mine, that would be a problem in its own right.
“I was very worried because you hadn’t been sending any indirect messages.”
“I’ve been keeping away from ‘Star Stream broadcasting’ for a while.”
Looking closely, I noticed that the waves of energy from his whole body were far more refined than before. A thought suddenly struck me.
“Were you already on this island before this scenario began?”
“It has already been about fifteen years.”
······Fifteen years?
A sentence from Ways of Survival came to mind.
「‘Reincarnation Island’ is located within the <Star Stream>’s Dark Fault.」
It had been three years by Earth’s time, but time flowed several times faster within the Dark Fault. That was precisely why Kyrgios and Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had frequented this place.
The island’s current time density seemed to differ from Earth’s by roughly a factor of five.
“Could your reason for staying here have been······?”
Cheok Jungyeong nodded.
“An ‘Outer God’ or not, I couldn’t even handle a single avatar.”
A scene flashed through my mind.
Three years earlier, on the day the seventy-third Demon Realm fell.
Facing that calamity, Cheok Jungyeong had lost his incarnation body.

Proud as he was, he must have been greatly shocked to learn that this world held something so far beyond him that he could not cut it. That made this all the more surprising. Other constellations had their very sense of self shattered by merely facing that calamity. Yet he still thought only of tearing it apart and killing it.
Perhaps this was the theme of the constellation known as Goryeo’s First Sword.
“I thought I should train again, starting with the most basic things. This island is an excellent place for that.”
As he spoke, Cheok Jungyeong looked at the people cutting through the undergrowth ahead.
People moving lightly even in the hot, sticky forest.
They were probably this island’s Forgotten People.
Perhaps noticing my gaze, one of them spoke.
“You did well to survive. Usually, constellations from outside lose their heads in less than an hour. Ah, except for ‘Monster Cheok’ over there, of course.”
“Thank you for helping us. My name is Kim Dokja.”
I deliberately omitted my modifier.
Many of the first generation’s Forgotten People considered modifiers mere bluster.
Apparently pleased with my answer, the man grinned.
“I forgot my name long ago. Everyone ends up that way if they stay here.”
With that, he bounded ahead.
The Forgotten People. Those who had forgotten their own names after countless reincarnations.
But they hadn’t truly forgotten their names. Remembering the past had simply become too painful.
An ancient air emanated from the Forgotten People as they strode ahead, clearing a path. Very robust Stories, honed with painstaking devotion.
Lee Jihye whispered,
“How are they so strong?”
It was only natural to wonder.
The Status I could sense from them wasn’t particularly impressive.
Yet they had killed the troll we’d struggled against with a single slash.
“We seem to have more Stories, and better ones, too······.”
“No matter how many good Stories you have, if you can’t use them properly, they’re no better than idle tales.”
Lee Jihye looked at me as though asking what I meant.
Just as I was about to continue, Cheok Jungyeong cut in.
“He is right. Even with ten fine swords, a human can properly hold no more than two.”
Goryeo’s First Sword, indeed. His body was a sword, his mind was a sword, and even his analogies were swords.
As though she’d gained some profound enlightenment, Lee Jihye looked down at her hands. Meanwhile, Cheok Jungyeong regarded me thoughtfully and spoke.
“You’ve gathered many excellent Stories. In terms of Status alone, even high-ranking constellations would not outclass you now.”
“You flatter me.”
“But······ you’ve accumulated too many in too short a time. You know what state you’re in now, don’t you?”
I fell silent.
To him, my current state must have looked terribly precarious.
[The Giant Story ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’ is targeting your incarnation body.]
[The Story ‘One Who Opposes the Extraordinary’ doubts your qualifications!]
[The Story ‘One Who Killed an Outer God’ is dissatisfied with you.]

He was right. Earlier, I’d almost had my mind seized by my Stories after drawing on a Giant Story carelessly. If that had happened, I would have ended up exactly like the constellations I’d met at the ‘Duet between Good and Evil.’
“Descendant, do not forget. After a being creates a Story, the Story creates the being.”
I knew.
And because I knew, I had come to this island.
“I’ll keep that in mind.”
Before long, we arrived at the village.
[You have reached the first safe zone!]
[You are the 133rd to fulfill the ‘Small Island’ main scenario’s clear conditions!]
[You have fulfilled the hidden scenario’s clear conditions!]
[You have been added to the additional reward list for killing a powerful competitor.]
[Additional reward details are being prepared.]
The village was peaceful. Passing through the main gate, I saw a fairly well-organized community built around an enormous furnace at its center.
A woman in shabby clothes was feeding a cow, and a brawny, shaggy-bearded man was taking down laundry. There were also children who looked younger than Gilyoung and Yoosung.
A rural scene so tranquil it was hard to believe this was a village of the first generation’s Forgotten People.
「(······This place is really amazing.)」
‘Yoo Sangah-ssi?’
「(Oh, I’m sorry. Did I startle you by speaking so suddenly?)」
‘No. Is it all right for you to talk now?’
「(Yes, I’m on a short break. Sabyeogi seems busy, too.)」
For some reason, Yoo Sangah’s voice felt much closer than usual.
With the [Fourth Wall] thinner, perhaps her activities had become easier, too.
「(This village······ it’s like a mural painted by countless artisans over many years······.)」
Listening as she searched for the right words, I was inwardly impressed.
It looked ordinary, but as Yoo Sangah said, the village’s true nature was anything but.
I could tell just from the residents continuing their daily lives despite my arrival.
Bored looks, as though they had seen scenes like this hundreds, even thousands of times.
[Fuck, I nearly died.]
[What an insane island······. Were those really orcs?]
When I heard True Voices coming from somewhere, I turned and saw a group of constellations entering through the entrance on the opposite side of the village.
I quickly scanned their faces. Unfortunately, none of my companions were among the new arrivals.
Instead, I saw someone unwelcome.
[The Demon King ‘Eyes that See the Forbidden’ glares at you.]
A Demon King with the appearance of a black leopard and burning eyes.
I had seen him when I visited the 1863rd round.
The ruler of the sixty-fourth Demon Realm.
Eyes that See the Forbidden, Flauros.
······If I remembered correctly, he had died to Yoo Joonghyuk’s fist in the 1863rd round.
Apparently, this Demon King had also chosen this island to follow me.
After glaring at me with a strange look, Flauros smacked his lips and turned away.
His face was so transparent that I didn’t need to make any effort to read it.
He had probably decided this wasn’t an advantageous place for him to fight.
He must also have been quite wary of Cheok Jungyeong beside me.
I glanced at Cheok Jungyeong, who remained by my side.
“······Is there something you wish to say?”
“Nothing.”
······What excellent, dependable shoulders. I envied him.
[Is that it for this scenario? Hey, NPCs. Give us directions!]
As constellations entered one after another, the village grew increasingly noisy.
Amid the disturbances breaking out everywhere, one resident frowned and answered.
“······This is the end of the Small Island.”
[What an unhelpful tone. Well, that’s a scenario made by dokkaebi bastards for you.]
Perhaps reassured that there were no more monsters, the constellations were growing arrogant again.
[The Story ‘Be Weak before the Strong and Strong before the Weak’ begins its story.]
The voices of Stories flowing from the sinister constellations’ eyes.
······Cheok Jungyeong was right after all.
Constellation or incarnation, no matter how many years we had lived, there were no exceptions.
If we didn’t properly live our Stories, our Stories would live us.
[Are there no extra rewards here?]
[Should we search some houses? There might be a hidden piece or something.]
Sensing that things were about to become tiresome, the residents answered in weary voices.
“There’s nothing like that. The Small Island scenario is over. Anyone who wants to go to the next scenario, enter the furnace in the village center. That’s the portal.”
Just as some constellations frowned at the cold tone, the Demon King Flauros stepped forward.
[You’re noisy for a mere NPC. I decide when I leave this place.]
Apparently looking for someone to take his anger out on, he had already begun quietly raising his Status and speaking in True Voice.
[Having finally found a village, there is nothing wrong with resting a while. You there, bring out liquor and food! I am very hungry.]
A dozen or so constellations snickered at the words imbued with violent Status.
Frowning, Lee Jihye stepped forward.
“That bastard—”
“Wait.”
There probably wouldn’t be any room for us to intervene in this fight.
Indeed, the villagers showed no sign of being intimidated by the Demon King’s threats.
The man hanging laundry yawned as though bored and muttered casually,
“NPC this, NPC that······. I heard youngsters these days think life is a game.”
An old man carrying a wooden pack frame spoke as well.
“Always looking for some fortuitous encounter······. No passion. No passion at all······.”
The woman feeding the cow added her own words.
“Hock, ptui. This is why I opposed opening our island. I don’t care how badly we need coins. Why should I have to watch scum like that roll in? I’d rather raise a few more cows.”
Casual words, yet voices that reached us with absolute clarity.
As the situation took a strange turn, the constellations began watching warily.
Flauros roared.
[You vermin. What do you all think you’re······?]
Then a little kid sucking on candy right in front of him spoke.
“You’re the vermin, you brat who hasn’t even lived a thousand years.”
Flauros’ jaw dropped. As a being who reigned as the sixty-fourth Demon King, his reaction was only natural. It must have been the first insult of its kind in his life.
An evil smile briefly crossed his face.
[······The scenario never said not to kill NPCs.]
The powerful hostility radiating from the Demon King. The instant he growled and bared his fangs, every villager looked at him at once.
The man doing laundry.
The woman feeding the cow.
The old man carrying the wooden pack frame.
Gazes that seemed to freeze the entire world.
Sensing a strange current in the air, the constellations hesitated.
So did Flauros. He was a fairly experienced Demon King, so he would have begun to notice something was wrong. Perhaps he was thinking this.
「What the hell are these people?」
But there was no way he would back down now.
His pride as a Demon King wouldn’t allow him to be cowed by the residents of a tiny village.
In the end, he chose to make an example of the one who looked weakest.
[Die!]
Flauros’ claws shot toward the little kid sucking on candy in front of him.
But that was precisely the wrong choice.
「He clenched his fist. And then his fist was there.」
Then came the sound of something exploding.
Fragments of an incarnation body scattering through the air like fireworks.
Flauros’ headless incarnation body slowly sank to the ground.
[The Demon King ‘Eyes that See the Forbidden’ has been eliminated from the scenario.]
Having witnessed a Demon King’s death right before their eyes, the constellations backed away, trembling.
[Wh-what is this?]

The residents barely reacted to the constellations’ shock. The atmosphere was calm, as though no one would hold a funeral for a bug. The brawny man returned to his laundry, and the woman fed her cow. The old man shook his head and set to work on the firewood.
The child sucking candy spoke.
“Get out, all of you. I’m sick of looking at you.”
Pale-faced incarnations and constellations hastily fled to the portal.
The ‘Small Island’ scenario was already over. There was no reason to hesitate any longer.
After they disappeared through the portal one by one, fewer than ten constellations remained.
[The Giant Story ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’ wants you to move to the next scenario!]
My Giant Story had been reacting violently from the moment I faced that child.
It had probably noticed something, too.
Smiling wryly, I approached the child who had burst the Demon King’s head open.
[The Giant Story ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’ threatens you!]
I hadn’t expected Flauros to be helpful.
He had saved me the trouble of searching.
[The Giant Story ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’ declares that it will destroy your incarnation body if you approach him any further!]
Regardless, I ignored it and continued forward. The rampaging Giant Story released a threatening current into the surroundings.
Perhaps taking it as a provocation, the child looked at me with a flash of irritation.
“What? Do you want to end up like that guy?”
“One Invincible Fist (一拳無敵), Yoo Hoseong. You’re still every bit as skilled as when you taught Breaking the Sky Sword Saint and Kyrgios.”
The child’s expression changed.
All the residents here were ‘reincarnators.’ Their appearance gave no indication of their age.
The child before me, too, was a reincarnator who had lived for at least ten thousand years.
Narrowing his eyes, he asked me,
“······Who are you? What is your relationship with those children?”
[The Giant Story ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’ bares its teeth at the being before you.]
Another reason I had come to ‘Reincarnation Island.’
Considering the battles against Myth-grade constellations to come, there was something I absolutely had to obtain here.
Swallowing the blood rising in my throat, I spoke in a bloodshot voice.
“One Invincible Fist, please teach me ‘Story Control.’”
